IntervalNote: Effectively random failure. Shape 1.05 means scheduled replacement buys almost nothing -- replacing it early replaces a good part with an equally failure-prone new one.
Capacity fade. Deep discharge on high-payload profiles accelerates it well beyond what the hour meter suggests.
Servo and slip-ring wear. Nearly flat hazard: close to random failure, so condition monitoring earns less here than elsewhere.
Fatigue driven almost entirely by landing count rather than airborne time. The clearest case in the fleet for measuring cycles instead of hours.

Winding insulation and bearing degradation. Thermal cycling matters as much as running hours; the stress model has no temperature term, so cycling enters only through the per-landing cycle penalty and this interval is correspondingly approximate.
Bearing wear-out. Shape 2.6 means the failure rate rises steeply with accumulated stress -- the mean is a poor guide and the interval must be set on the distribution, not the average.
